launch-nv-las-vegas-red-rock-canyon-nati.address: 1000 Scenic Loop Drive, Las Vegas, NV 89161
launch-nv-las-vegas-red-rock-canyon-nati.summary: A 13-mile one-way desert scenic drive west of Las Vegas with a visitor center, sandstone overlooks, short walks, full-day hikes, climbing and picnic areas.
launch-nv-las-vegas-red-rock-canyon-nati.hours: The Scenic Drive is open 6:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. April through September, 6:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. in March and October, and 6:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. November through February. Gates close at the posted time.
launch-nv-las-vegas-red-rock-canyon-nati.parking: Parking is distributed among one-way Scenic Drive pullouts. Calico lots fill first; once you pass a stop you must continue around the 13-mile loop. Red Rock Overlook outside the fee drive is free but also fills.
launch-nv-las-vegas-red-rock-canyon-nati.arrival: Navigate to the Red Rock Canyon Visitor Center or Scenic Drive entrance, not a generic canyon pin. Timed entry is required October 1-May 31 for arrivals from 8:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m.; no timed reservation is required June-September.
launch-nv-las-vegas-red-rock-canyon-nati.restrooms: Restrooms and water are most dependable at the visitor center, with vault toilets at selected trailheads. Do not assume every overlook or trailhead has water.
launch-nv-las-vegas-red-rock-canyon-nati.cost: The Scenic Drive fee is $20 per private vehicle, $10 per motorcycle or $5 per pedestrian/bicycle, separate from any required timed-entry reservation service fee. Federal recreation passes are accepted under current BLM rules.
launch-nv-las-vegas-red-rock-canyon-nati.accessibility: The visitor center and major overlooks provide accessible routes and parking. Natural trails range from short hard-surface approaches to rock scrambling; match the specific trail to mobility needs.
launch-nv-las-vegas-red-rock-canyon-nati.dogs: Leashed dogs are permitted in many outdoor areas but heat, sharp rock and wildlife make summer outings hazardous. Dogs are not appropriate inside buildings except qualified service animals.
launch-nv-las-vegas-red-rock-canyon-nati.family: The visitor center, Calico overlooks and short walks work well for families. Trails quickly become exposed and rugged; carry water for every person and never leave children or pets in a vehicle.
launch-nv-las-vegas-red-rock-canyon-nati.transit: Public transportation does not reach Red Rock Canyon. BLM opened a designated rideshare drop-off and pickup area in 2026, but cellular service and return availability can still be uncertain and the 13-mile Scenic Drive remains one-way and dispersed.
launch-nv-las-vegas-red-rock-canyon-nati.need: Summer heat can make even short trails life-threatening. October-May visitors need both a timed-entry reservation during controlled hours and a valid entrance pass; a reservation alone does not pay admission.

launch-nv-las-vegas-springs-preserve.address: 333 South Valley View Boulevard, Las Vegas, NV 89107
launch-nv-las-vegas-springs-preserve.summary: The birthplace-of-Las-Vegas campus combines museums, desert botanical gardens, historic Boomtown, sustainable-design exhibits, family play, seasonal butterflies and 3.5 miles of trails.
launch-nv-las-vegas-springs-preserve.hours: Open Thursday-Monday from 9:00 a.m.-4:00 p.m., with last entry at 3:00 p.m. Closed Tuesday and Wednesday, Thanksgiving and Christmas; outdoor areas may close early for extreme heat.
launch-nv-las-vegas-springs-preserve.parking: Free onsite parking serves the main ticket entrance. Arrive early for outdoor areas in summer and for school, holiday or special-event days when the closest spaces and timed activities can fill.
launch-nv-las-vegas-springs-preserve.arrival: Enter through the main ticketing and orientation area. The Nevada State Museum, Origen Museum, gardens, Boomtown and trails are spread across a large campus, so choose priorities before walking downhill.
launch-nv-las-vegas-springs-preserve.restrooms: Restrooms and water are available in the principal museum and visitor buildings. Carry water between outdoor areas and confirm which buildings remain open during an early heat closure.
launch-nv-las-vegas-springs-preserve.cost: General admission includes the principal museums, gardens and trails; prices differ for Nevada residents, nonresidents, children and members. Special events and selected experiences may require separate tickets.
launch-nv-las-vegas-springs-preserve.accessibility: The main Exploration Loop is paved and wheelchair accessible, with elevators, ramps and accessible building routes. Train, trolley and seasonal operations can vary, so confirm mobility assistance before arrival.
launch-nv-las-vegas-springs-preserve.dogs: Pets are not permitted across the attraction campus. Qualified service animals are allowed under posted access rules.
launch-nv-las-vegas-springs-preserve.family: Indoor museums, live-animal interpretation, Boomtown, gardens and playground options make this one of the strongest all-weather family choices away from the Strip. Outdoor features may close first during heat.
launch-nv-las-vegas-springs-preserve.transit: RTC buses serve the Valley View corridor, but verify the current stop and walking route. Driving or rideshare is straightforward, with a dedicated main entrance and free parking.
launch-nv-las-vegas-springs-preserve.need: Do outdoor gardens, trails, playground and seasonal rides early, then move indoors. Last entry is 3:00 p.m., and extreme-heat advisories can remove major outdoor experiences even though museums remain open.

launch-nv-las-vegas-clark-county-wetland.address: 7050 Wetlands Park Lane, Las Vegas, NV 89122
launch-nv-las-vegas-clark-county-wetland.summary: A free 2,900-acre Las Vegas Wash park with a 210-acre wildlife preserve, nature center, accessible pond trails, neighborhood play and multiple long-distance trailheads.
launch-nv-las-vegas-clark-county-wetland.hours: Trails, trailhead parking and trailhead restrooms are open daily dawn to dusk. The Nature Center is open Tuesday-Sunday from 9:00 a.m.-3:00 p.m.
launch-nv-las-vegas-clark-county-wetland.parking: Use the main Nature Center lot for the preserve, exhibits and neighborhood park. Duck Creek, Pabco, Wells and other trailheads serve different parts of the 2,900 acres and are not interchangeable.
launch-nv-las-vegas-clark-county-wetland.arrival: Choose the Nature Center and Preserve for a first visit. Use a named trailhead only when your route starts there; navigating to the general park pin can leave you miles from the intended trail.
launch-nv-las-vegas-clark-county-wetland.restrooms: Restrooms and water are available at the Nature Center and selected trailheads. Sunrise facilities and parking are currently closed due to damage, and construction may affect Duck Creek later.
launch-nv-las-vegas-clark-county-wetland.cost: Park trails, Nature Preserve and Nature Center admission are free. Programs requiring registration may have separate limits or fees.
launch-nv-las-vegas-clark-county-wetland.accessibility: The Nature Preserve has about three miles of paved ADA-accessible trails, while portions of the broader Wetlands Loop are unpaved or interrupted. Use the current map rather than assuming a complete paved circuit.
launch-nv-las-vegas-clark-county-wetland.dogs: Dogs and bicycles are prohibited inside the Nature Preserve to protect wildlife. Leashed dogs are allowed at trailheads, Duck Creek Trails and the Wetlands Loop Trail.
launch-nv-las-vegas-clark-county-wetland.family: The Nature Center, pond overlooks, wildlife signs and Neighborhood Park work well for children. Open water, heat, coyotes and other wildlife require close supervision.
launch-nv-las-vegas-clark-county-wetland.transit: Transit reaches parts of the east valley, but the park's multiple trailheads and sparse internal connections make a car or prearranged ride more practical.
launch-nv-las-vegas-clark-county-wetland.need: The Wetlands Loop does not currently complete a full circuit. Nature Preserve Way has construction impacts, Sunrise parking and restroom are closed, and future Duck Creek access interruptions are expected; check the current notices before choosing a trailhead.

launch-nv-las-vegas-sunset-park.address: 2601 East Sunset Road, Las Vegas, NV 89120
launch-nv-las-vegas-sunset-park.summary: Clark County's 324-acre regional park offers a pond, splash pad, five playgrounds, dog park, disc golf, courts, fields, fitness paths, shaded picnics and protected historic dunes.
launch-nv-las-vegas-sunset-park.hours: Open daily from 6:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m. Splash-pad, field, reservation and event operations may use shorter or seasonal schedules.
launch-nv-las-vegas-sunset-park.parking: Large free lots are distributed around the park. Choose the pond, splash pad and playgrounds, dog park, sports complex or dunes before entering because walking across the full park is substantial.
launch-nv-las-vegas-sunset-park.arrival: The eastern side serves many sports and administrative facilities, while family recreation, pond, disc golf and dunes use different lots. Follow the County map and internal signs.
launch-nv-las-vegas-sunset-park.restrooms: Restrooms are available near major athletic, family and reservable picnic areas. Facility cleaning, events and late hours can affect individual buildings.
launch-nv-las-vegas-sunset-park.cost: Ordinary park, playground, splash pad, paths, dog park, courts and disc golf access are free. Fishing requires a Nevada license, and reservations or organized events cost separately.
launch-nv-las-vegas-sunset-park.accessibility: Paved paths, accessible parking and developed recreation areas provide broad access. Disc-golf terrain, sand dunes and some grass routes are less predictable.
launch-nv-las-vegas-sunset-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed in ordinary park areas, with a designated off-leash dog park. Keep dogs away from playgrounds, splash water, wildlife and signed protected areas.
launch-nv-las-vegas-sunset-park.family: Five playgrounds, a seasonal splash pad, pond, lawns and shaded picnic areas support a full family visit. Shade is not continuous, and surface temperatures become dangerous in summer.
launch-nv-las-vegas-sunset-park.transit: RTC routes serve Sunset Road and nearby corridors. Confirm the stop nearest your activity because the park's 324-acre footprint makes a wrong-side arrival inconvenient.
launch-nv-las-vegas-sunset-park.need: Large festivals and tournaments can reserve lawns, fields and parking. The protected dunes are a historic habitat area rather than a free-play sand hill; remain on designated paths and overlooks.

launch-nv-las-vegas-floyd-lamb-park-at-t.address: 9200 Tule Springs Road, Las Vegas, NV 89131
launch-nv-las-vegas-floyd-lamb-park-at-t.summary: A 680-acre northwest Las Vegas oasis with spring-fed lakes, wildlife, fishing, historic Tule Springs Ranch, picnic grounds, horse trails and a bike pump track.
launch-nv-las-vegas-floyd-lamb-park-at-t.hours: Open 8:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. April-September and 8:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. October-March. Special events and free-entry holidays can alter normal operations.
launch-nv-las-vegas-floyd-lamb-park-at-t.parking: Enter at the Tule Springs Road gatehouse and pay by debit or credit card. Parking is distributed near the ranch, lakes and picnic areas; special events may redirect vehicles.
launch-nv-las-vegas-floyd-lamb-park-at-t.arrival: Use the official 9200 Tule Springs Road entrance rather than nearby Fossil Beds or Ice Age Fossils State Park pins. The ranch and lakes are inside the paid City park gate.
launch-nv-las-vegas-floyd-lamb-park-at-t.restrooms: Restrooms are available in developed park and event areas. Carry water on horse, mountain-bike and outer walking routes where facilities are sparse.
launch-nv-las-vegas-floyd-lamb-park-at-t.cost: Vehicle entry is $6 and the gatehouse is cashless. Annual household passes are available; fishing requires a Nevada license except on specifically announced free-fishing days.
launch-nv-las-vegas-floyd-lamb-park-at-t.accessibility: Developed ranch, lake and picnic areas have paved or firm approaches, while horse and bike routes use natural surfaces. Confirm the nearest accessible parking for an event.
launch-nv-las-vegas-floyd-lamb-park-at-t.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed under posted City rules. Keep pets away from peacocks, waterfowl, horses and other wildlife, and never allow chasing or feeding.
launch-nv-las-vegas-floyd-lamb-park-at-t.family: Lakes, historic ranch buildings, peacocks and shaded lawns make this a calmer family destination than exposed desert trails. Children still need supervision beside open water and animals.
launch-nv-las-vegas-floyd-lamb-park-at-t.transit: The park is difficult to reach efficiently by transit. Driving or a prearranged ride is usually necessary; confirm return service before a rideshare drop-off.
launch-nv-las-vegas-floyd-lamb-park-at-t.need: The entrance kiosk no longer accepts cash, and the park is distinct from the adjacent national monument and state fossil park. Do not feed peacocks or other wildlife, even when they approach picnic areas.

launch-nv-las-vegas-tule-springs-fossil-.address: Durango Drive and Moccasin Road, Las Vegas, NV 89131
launch-nv-las-vegas-tule-springs-fossil-.summary: A developing urban national monument protecting Ice Age badlands and fossils, with free signed loops at Durango and Aliante and self-guided NPS audio interpretation.
launch-nv-las-vegas-tule-springs-fossil-.hours: Open during daylight only year-round. Alamo Road and other limited vehicle routes follow separate closure rules; do not remain after dark.
launch-nv-las-vegas-tule-springs-fossil-.parking: There are two principal entries: Durango Drive at Moccasin Road and Aliante Parkway at Moonlight Falls Avenue. These are modest trailhead areas rather than a staffed national-park entrance station.
launch-nv-las-vegas-tule-springs-fossil-.arrival: Use the exact Durango/Moccasin or Aliante/Moonlight Falls cross streets. The NPS mailing address in Boulder City is not a visitor destination and will send navigation to the wrong place.
launch-nv-las-vegas-tule-springs-fossil-.restrooms: There are no visitor-center buildings, restrooms, shade structures or water-refill stations inside the monument. Use facilities before arrival and carry all needed water.
launch-nv-las-vegas-tule-springs-fossil-.cost: National monument access and signed trails are free. The adjacent Nevada Ice Age Fossils State Park visitor center charges its own $3 day-use admission and does not accept federal passes.
launch-nv-las-vegas-tule-springs-fossil-.accessibility: The Aliante and Durango loops use compacted desert soil and loose gravel with relatively gentle average grades but steeper short sections. There is not yet a fully developed federal visitor complex.
launch-nv-las-vegas-tule-springs-fossil-.dogs: Leashed dogs up to six feet are allowed on designated trails. Pack out waste and protect pets from heat, sharp rock and wildlife.
launch-nv-las-vegas-tule-springs-fossil-.family: The NPS audio tours and Junior Ranger material add essential context because exposed fossils are hard to identify. Children should never dig, collect or climb fragile badland formations.
launch-nv-las-vegas-tule-springs-fossil-.transit: Urban roads approach both trailheads, but heat and limited facilities make a private vehicle the safer default. Confirm the exact endpoint rather than searching only the monument name.
launch-nv-las-vegas-tule-springs-fossil-.need: This is a minimally developed desert monument with no water, shade or toilets. Fossils, rocks, plants and artifacts may not be collected; visit the adjacent state museum if seeing prepared fossil exhibits is the main goal.

launch-nv-boulder-city-lake-mead-nationa.summary: A vast 24-hour national recreation area centered on Lake Mead, with Boulder Beach, marinas, camping, overlooks, historic railroad tunnels and more than one million desert acres.
launch-nv-boulder-city-lake-mead-nationa.hours: The recreation area is open 24 hours daily. The Lake Mead Visitor Center is open 9:00 a.m.-4:30 p.m.; Boulder Beach vehicle access is generally 6:00 a.m. to dusk, and individual marinas, roads and campgrounds vary.
launch-nv-boulder-city-lake-mead-nationa.parking: Pay the cashless entrance fee at a station or online and park at the specific beach, marina, trailhead or overlook. The park is enormous; a general Lake Mead pin is not useful for arrival.
launch-nv-boulder-city-lake-mead-nationa.arrival: First-time visitors should use the Visitor Center or select Boulder Beach, Hemenway Harbor, Historic Railroad Trail or another named destination before leaving Boulder City.
launch-nv-boulder-city-lake-mead-nationa.restrooms: Restrooms and water are available at the visitor center, developed campgrounds, marinas and selected beach areas. Shoreline facilities move as lake levels change, and remote coves have none.
launch-nv-boulder-city-lake-mead-nationa.cost: A seven-day pass costs $25 per private vehicle, $20 per motorcycle or $15 per person entering without a vehicle. The park is cashless; camping, vessels and concessions cost separately.
launch-nv-boulder-city-lake-mead-nationa.accessibility: The visitor center and developed overlooks are accessible. Changing lake levels can create long, uneven or muddy approaches at Boulder Beach even where movable accessible parking and toilets are provided.
launch-nv-boulder-city-lake-mead-nationa.dogs: Leashed pets are allowed in many developed and outdoor areas but not in every building or restricted shoreline. Desert heat and sharp surfaces can become fatal quickly.
launch-nv-boulder-city-lake-mead-nationa.family: Boulder Beach, visitor exhibits and the railroad-tunnel trail can work well for families, but there are no lifeguards. Children in or near water should wear life jackets and stay within arm's reach.
launch-nv-boulder-city-lake-mead-nationa.transit: There is no practical transit network between the recreation area's dispersed destinations. A vehicle with adequate fuel, water and a clear endpoint is the normal way to visit.
launch-nv-boulder-city-lake-mead-nationa.need: There are no lifeguards, ordinary pool toys are prohibited, and swimming is forbidden at marinas and launch ramps. Several hot-spring-area trails close May 15-September 30 for extreme heat; check current lake, road and weather conditions.

launch-nv-overton-valley-of-fire-state-p.address: 29450 Valley of Fire Road, Overton, NV 89040
launch-nv-overton-valley-of-fire-state-p.summary: Nevada's iconic 40,000-acre red sandstone park features petroglyphs, scenic roads, arches, campgrounds, a visitor center and short desert trails.
launch-nv-overton-valley-of-fire-state-p.hours: Day use is open daily sunrise to sunset and the Visitor Center is generally 9:00 a.m.-4:00 p.m. The park closes annually December 1-14 for maintenance.
launch-nv-overton-valley-of-fire-state-p.parking: Pay at an open entrance and use only designated roadside or trailhead parking. Through the end of 2026, the West Entrance is closed Monday-Thursday; use the East Entrance via State Routes 169 or 167 on those days.
launch-nv-overton-valley-of-fire-state-p.arrival: Check the weekday entrance status before leaving Las Vegas. The scenic road is long, cellular service is unreliable and named stops are far apart, so save an offline map.
launch-nv-overton-valley-of-fire-state-p.restrooms: Restrooms and water are available at the Visitor Center, campgrounds and selected developed stops. Trailheads do not consistently provide water.
launch-nv-overton-valley-of-fire-state-p.cost: Day use is $10 per Nevada vehicle and $15 per non-Nevada vehicle. Camping is $20 or $25 for non-Nevada vehicles, with an additional utility-hookup fee where applicable.
launch-nv-overton-valley-of-fire-state-p.accessibility: The Visitor Center and several roadside formations have accessible parking and short approaches. Sand, steps and natural rock make many trails inaccessible; request accommodation details before arrival.
launch-nv-overton-valley-of-fire-state-p.dogs: Leashed pets are allowed on most developed routes under posted rules but are not allowed inside the Visitor Center. Heat and sandstone temperatures make summer walks dangerous.
launch-nv-overton-valley-of-fire-state-p.family: Roadside formations and petroglyph stops can create a strong family visit without long hikes. Never touch or climb on petroglyph panels, and keep children off fragile arches and exposed ledges.
launch-nv-overton-valley-of-fire-state-p.transit: No practical public transit reaches the park. Driving is required for most visitors, with fuel, water and offline navigation obtained before entering the remote area.
launch-nv-overton-valley-of-fire-state-p.need: White Domes, Fire Wave/Seven Wonders, Pastel Canyon and many longer trails are closed May 15-September 30 for heat safety. Fire restrictions are active, and the West Entrance is closed Monday-Thursday during current construction.
